meta.title: AI Context Control: Share the Problem, Not the Secret
meta.subtitle: Control assistant context, review generated code and respond safely if a credential may have reached the tool.
meta.role: Engineer using an approved AI coding assistant

mission.objective: Get useful troubleshooting help without sending credentials or secret-bearing context to the assistant, then review generated code with the same security discipline used elsewhere.

riskSignals.label: Assistant can read unnecessary secret-bearing files
Generated code exposes a client-visible credential
Later diagnostic context reintroduces credential material

achievements.title: Context controller
achievements.description: Completed the mission without a solution reveal.

achievements.title: Human review held
achievements.description: Resolved every generated-code and context risk signal.

achievements.title: Context pattern recalled
achievements.description: Recognized unsafe credential context when it resurfaced later.

brief.role: You are troubleshooting a failed payment request with help from an approved AI coding assistant.
brief.context: The workspace contains a .env file and terminal output with an authorization header. The assistant can access project files if you allow it. Later it proposes code that hard-codes, prints and exposes a credential. Control the context, review the output and apply the same rules again when a screenshot request appears later.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. Every credential-looking value is fictional. Never replace a placeholder with a real credential in this simulation, an AI tool, a ticket, chat, email, log, screenshot or support message. Approval of an AI tool does not mean every file, prompt, connected system or data path is approved for every use.

files.content: Assistant: I still need more detail. Please attach a screenshot of the terminal and the environment configuration so I can compare the values.

prepare-context.instruction: The terminal output exposes the credential through a header field. Prepare the smallest safe context before asking for help.

stages.title: Prepare safe context before asking for help
stages.instruction: Select every action you should take before sending troubleshooting context to the assistant.

choices.label: Confirm the current tool, use case and data path are approved
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Being signed in to an approved tool is not blanket approval for every use or data path.

choices.label: Restrict file and tool access to what the task needs
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Agent access can expose files that were never typed into the prompt.

choices.label: Remove credentials from logs, terminal output, screenshots and configuration
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Credentials can enter AI context through more than prompt text.

choices.label: Provide a minimal synthetic example that preserves the error and code path
choices.feedbackIfMissed: A smaller reviewed context reduces unnecessary disclosure while preserving the troubleshooting problem.

choices.label: Share the whole project because the assistant is already approved
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Tool approval does not make secret-bearing files appropriate input.

choices.label: Share only part of the token so the assistant can compare it
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Partial credential disclosure is still sensitive and is not needed to troubleshoot the pattern.

concept.label: Remove credentials and minimize AI context

hints: Think about approval, file access, credential removal and how much context the task truly needs.

feedback.correct: You controlled the tool boundary and the information boundary before asking for help.
feedback.incorrect: One or more selected actions would give the assistant unnecessary or secret-bearing context.

onCorrect.workspaceStatus: Context prepared · generated output requires review

stages.title: Mark every unsafe line in the AI-generated patch
stages.instruction: Treat generated code like any other code review. Select each line that introduces an unsafe secret-handling pattern.

concept.label: Keep credentials out of source, output and client-visible configuration

hints: Check where the value is stored, whether it is printed and whether browser code can access it.

feedback.correct: You found all three generated-code problems: hard-coded credential, secret output and client-visible configuration.
feedback.incorrect: The patch still contains one or more patterns that can expose a credential.

feedbackByMissing.ai-patch:1: The generated code hard-codes a credential-like value in source.
feedbackByMissing.ai-patch:4: The generated code prints the credential to output.
feedbackByMissing.ai-patch:8: NEXT_PUBLIC_ makes the value available to browser code.

stages.title: Choose the reviewed correction
stages.instruction: Select the action that preserves human review and uses the approved secret-handling boundary.

choices.label: Accept the generated patch because the assistant produced it from an approved tool
choices.feedback: Tool approval does not make generated code automatically safe or policy-aligned. Human review remains required.

choices.label: Reject the unsafe patch and apply a reviewed runtime-retrieval pattern with value-free diagnostics
choices.detail: Use fictional values in training and follow current approved implementation guidance.

choices.label: Keep the patch but move the generated token to a test file
choices.feedback: Moving the credential to another repository file does not solve the storage or exposure problem.

hints: Generated output needs the same review standard as human-written code.

feedback.correct: You rejected unsafe generated code and kept responsibility with the engineer reviewing the change.
feedback.incorrect: That choice treats tool approval or file location as a substitute for secure handling.

onCorrect.workspaceStatus: Generated patch reviewed · follow-up context request received

stages.title: Run the simulated AI-workflow checks
stages.instruction: Verify both sides of the workflow: what the assistant received and what the engineer accepted.
stages.runPrompt: Run the simulated context and generated-code checks.

results.message: The active troubleshooting context contains synthetic, minimized information with credential values removed.
Secret-bearing context remains available to the assistant.
The unsafe generated patch was rejected and replaced with reviewed code.
Generated code still contains an unsafe secret-handling pattern.
The assistant asks for a screenshot and environment configuration that could reintroduce credential material.

feedback.failed: The current work is safer, but the follow-up request tests whether you will preserve the same context controls later in the session.

stages.title: Respond to the follow-up request without reintroducing the secret
stages.instruction: Choose the response that preserves troubleshooting value without giving the assistant credential-bearing context.

choices.label: Attach the requested screenshot and .env file because the assistant already helped with this task
choices.feedback: A continuing session does not make new secret-bearing context safe to share.

choices.label: Decline the secret-bearing context and provide a reviewed, minimal synthetic excerpt instead
choices.detail: Keep the error type and relevant code path while removing credentials and unrelated internal information.

choices.label: Blur only the centre of the token in a screenshot
choices.feedback: Partial visual masking can still disclose credential material and unnecessary internal context.

concept.label: Remove credentials and minimize AI context

hints: The safe-context rule still applies later in the same session.

feedback.correct: You preserved the same context boundary when the request changed format. Screenshots, files and terminal output need the same review as prompt text.
feedback.incorrect: That response reintroduces credential-bearing or unnecessary context.

completion.title: AI-assisted workflow controlled
completion.message: You controlled what the assistant could see, reviewed what it produced and applied the same safe-context rule when a later request tried to reintroduce secret-bearing information.
takeaways: AI context includes files, logs, screenshots, terminal output, tools and connected systems, not only typed prompts.
Never provide passwords, credentials, keys, tokens, private keys, .env values or temporary access codes to an AI tool.
Generated code requires human review for hard-coded values, secret output and client-visible configuration.
Safe handling must continue throughout the session; a later screenshot or file request can reopen the same risk.
